Risk (oracle audit of the round's diff, finding 1; not fixed here): `CheckPod` (operatorpod.go) fences an operator mount only against `legionMountPaths()` and `imageOwnedPaths()`, neither naming /home/legion/.local/state; before 5f9f08fe nothing wrote there, now every role's shim must `MkdirAll` under it, so an operator `pod.volume_mounts` entry at /home/legion/.local or /home/legion/.local/state backed by a read-only Secret or ConfigMap passes `--check-config` and then refuses every role's start (`pod safety: make Oh My Pi's state directory …: read-only file system`, the shim's exit line naming the directory) until the claims' launch attempts run out. Same class as XDG_CACHE_HOME and XDG_DATA_HOME, which are not fenced either; a decision for the architect whether to add the state home to the fence.

Risk (oracle audit, finding 2; proven here, pinned nowhere durable): the fix rests on Oh My Pi resolving its state root to $XDG_STATE_HOME/omp/profiles/<profile> only where that directory exists. It holds in the pinned 18.6.0 (read in the binary: the `Xhe` directory resolver's existence check per XDG variable, the agent-dir override ignored under a named profile) and the live run here proves it, but no unit test ports the state-root rule (internal/ompdirs ports the data root only, after pi-utils 18.1.21) and stage 4a's pod-baseline asserts the variable and `test -d` of the directory the shim made, not a directory Oh My Pi wrote under it (its `logs/` or `run/daemons/`); a pin bump that moved the rule would return the shared lock silently. Worth a `logs/`-exists assertion in pod-baseline or a port in ompdirs, at the architect's call.

Nits from the audit for the Fast-follow line: stage4b-sandbox-tree.sh:161-163 `override_memory[tester]=4Gi` now equals the raised default, so the tester row no longer tells a file-set memory from the default (the reviewer row still does; the example's reviewer override was moved to 6Gi for this reason, the script's was not), and docs/kubernetes.md:708's `tester: { cpu: 1, memory: 4Gi }  # both fields set` has the same drift; docs/kubernetes.md's debugging recipe (`kubectl exec -c <role> -- sh`) lands in a shell without the role's XDG_STATE_HOME, so an operator looking for the live agent's Oh My Pi logs under ~/.omp/profiles/legion finds none — one sentence naming /home/legion/.local/state/<role>; `### Volume retention` and the new re-admission paragraph sit under the `## Kubernetes runtime (TypeScript daemon)` heading, which calls its contents retired.

Audit findings read as not defects: ensureSandbox's one policy holds for a daemon's run because the boot census (`CensusLegacyIssueSandboxes`, run once from `clusterCheck` and refusing the daemon's start) is the only guard against a Sandbox without a volume, so a Sandbox made by hand with the project label after boot would be adopted and its pod wait on a PVC that never comes until the boot timeout, every retry alike (the removed branch deleted and recreated it); the relabel-vs-CleanupTree interleaving is self-healing at the cost of one boot timeout, as the design documents; `deleteSandbox` is foreground for both its callers (as before: CleanupTree passed `true`), while the orphan sweep's `deleteFenced` stays background by design and its live check polls for the PVC.

This tester pod still runs the tree-volume layout of the deployed daemon: nproc 8 and MemTotal 62 GiB with no reservation, the three live roles' containers sharing one network namespace, which is what made the per-role state-home control possible here.
